# Yundera/AppStore — OpenClaw

**Audit date:** 2026-08-05 · **Store version:** `alpine/openclaw:2026.2.2` (sidecar `ghcr.io/yundera/nginx-hash-lock:1.0.5`) · **Compose blob sha:** `c7820fcd` (`Apps/OpenClaw/docker-compose.yml.disabled` @ `main`)
**VERDICT: NON-COMPLIANT · Critical · risk_score 232**
Depth `full` · Scope `n-a` (audit, no `compose_base`) · Demo host selected: **demostaging2.inojob.com** (✅ Ready, 19.9h remaining — the most of the pool)
App KB fixture: `NeFOTSJPGH` — last verified 2026-08-05.

## Headline

`Apps/OpenClaw/` ships **no **`docker-compose.yml`** at **`main` — the directory contains only `docker-compose.yml.disabled`, `icon.png` and `screenshot-1.png`. CONTRIBUTING.md requires every app directory to contain a `docker-compose.yml`, so the app is currently **parked**: it cannot be indexed, listed or installed by the store. Judged on the merits of the disabled compose, it additionally carries **two Critical defects** that must be fixed before it is re-enabled.

History note: `b7fcb72e` (2026-02-16) renamed `docker-compose.yml.disabled` → `docker-compose.yml`, and that commit *is* an ancestor of `main`; the file was subsequently reverted to `.disabled` by later history. Verified twice at `ref=main` (contents API listing + `raw.githubusercontent.com` returning HTTP 404 for `docker-compose.yml`).

## Tech & Documentation (Static leaf `LPwfKYUVig`)

### Failing items

| # | Item | Severity | Rule | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Data Persistence — "No Data Erasure" | **Critical** | — | `pre-install-cmd` runs `cat > /DATA/AppData/openclaw/openclaw.json << 'OCEOF'`, which **unconditionally truncates and rewrites the app's main config file on every install — including every reinstall and upgrade**. CONTRIBUTING requires "Container startup processes must never erase or overwrite existing user data" and "Use initialization scripts that check for existing data before creating defaults". The app's own `tips.before_install` instructs the user to add their Anthropic/OpenAI API key "in the Config section", i.e. into exactly this file. This is the static counterpart of Functional Phase G and is the same defect class as the FileBrowser non-idempotent `pre-install-cmd` precedent. Fix: guard with `[ -f … ] |
| C2 | Security — auth enabled **and documented** | **Critical** | — | The backend deliberately disables its own auth: `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_CONTROL_UI_DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_DEVICE_AUTH: "true"`, `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_CONTROL_UI_ALLOW_INSECURE_AUTH: "true"`, and `--allow-unconfigured` on the gateway command. The **only** remaining gate is the `nginx-hash-lock` perimeter sidecar keyed on a single shared secret that `x-casaos.index: /?hash=$AUTH_HASH&token=$AUTH_HASH` carries **in the URL query string** (leaks via browser history, referrer headers, proxy/access logs and screenshots). CONTRIBUTING mandates that an app shipping with authentication disabled **must** ship a `rationale.md`; **no **`rationale.md`** exists**. Blast radius is what makes this Critical rather than cosmetic: OpenClaw's own store description advertises "Shell commands: Execute scripts and system commands" and "File access: Read and write files on your system", so possession of the hash is effectively code execution inside the container. |
| M1 | Required file `docker-compose.yml` | **Major** | — | Absent at `main`; only `docker-compose.yml.disabled`. App is not installable or listable. This alone makes the three install-related Functionality checklist items (fresh install, uninstall/reinstall, upgrade) unverifiable by any means. |
| M2 | Required asset `thumbnail.png` | **Major** | — | Neither the file nor an `x-casaos.thumbnail` key exists. CONTRIBUTING marks `thumbnail.png` "(Required) Tile image shown in the AppStore listing". |
| M3 | Permissions / works-immediately | **Major** | **D4** | `pre-install-cmd` creates `/DATA/AppData/openclaw` and `openclaw.json` **as root** (`mkdir -p`, `chmod 644`), but `openclaw-backend` declares no `user:` field — and CONTRIBUTING is explicit that "if no `user` field is specified, the container will run as PUID:PGID". The backend (1000:1000) therefore receives a root-owned `0755` state directory containing a root-owned `0644` config, and cannot create or rewrite files in its own `/home/node/.openclaw`. CONTRIBUTING also states the App folder "should always be owned by `PUID:PGID`". Unverified at runtime (see Functionality) but a strong first-boot failure candidate, and a plausible reason the app was parked. |
| m1 | Volume and environment variable descriptions | **Minor** | — | `x-casaos` carries no per-volume or per-env descriptions, though the compose exposes user-facing knobs (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `TZ`) and one volume. Documentation checklist item. |
| m2 | Store-pattern drift | **Minor** | — | Uses the legacy single-label Caddy form (`caddy=openclaw-${APP_DOMAIN}` / `caddy.reverse_proxy`) with no `import gateway_tls` and no `nip.io` / `sslip.io` hosts, and the pre-rename `nginx-hash-lock:1.0.5` sidecar with no `container_name`, `hostname` or `OIDC_REGISTRAR_URL` — so no Authelia SSO. CONTRIBUTING now points at AppShield/OIDC (`Apps/ConvertX`, `Apps/Spliit`, `Apps/BrowserMCP`) as the reference deployment, and `container_name`/`hostname` are called "load-bearing" there. Consistent with the app being parked mid-`caddy migration preparation` (`a81d96c7`). |

### Passing items

- **No **`:latest` — both images pinned: `ghcr.io/yundera/nginx-hash-lock:1.0.5`, `alpine/openclaw:2026.2.2`. ✅
- `cpu_shares`** on every service** — `openclaw: 50`, `openclaw-backend: 90`, both at service top level (not under `deploy:`). ✅
- **Store App ID regex** — `name: openclaw` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`. ✅
- **Volumes under **`/DATA/AppData/<app>/` — the single mount is `/DATA/AppData/openclaw:/home/node/.openclaw`; nothing outside `/DATA`, no user directories touched. ✅
- **Permission strategy** — sidecar `user: "root"` mounts no volumes at all → **D1 pass** (rationale recommended, not required); backend defaults to `$PUID:$PGID` entirely within `/DATA` → **D4 pass**. (The *ownership* consequence is filed separately as M3.)
- **Static persistence mapping** — OpenClaw keeps config, sessions and memory under `~/.openclaw`; that entire state directory is mapped to `/DATA/AppData/openclaw`. No unmapped state location found, so the mapping check passes — the persistence risk here is erasure (C1), not an unmapped path. ✅
- **No hardcoded credentials** — all secrets are env-var references (`$AUTH_HASH`, `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}`, `${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}`); nothing baked. ✅
- `pre-install-cmd`** hygiene (partial)** — pulls no container image, so the no-`:latest` rule is moot; writes only to AppData, not a user directory, so `--user $PUID:$PGID` is not required. ✅ (Its *content* still fails under C1/M3.)
- **Asset URLs** — `icon.png` and `screenshot-1.png` both resolve to `cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Yundera/AppStore@main/...`, i.e. this repository, not a contributor fork. ✅
- **Description quality** — `x-casaos` supplies title, tagline, developer, author, category and a full description across six locales, plus `before_install` tips. ✅
- **Backend not publicly routed** — `openclaw-backend` carries no Caddy labels and sits on the internal `pcs` network; only the sidecar is reachable. ✅
**Static verdict:** `blocked` (two Critical, three Major, two Minor).

## Why the audit is NON-COMPLIANT and not ERRORED

The functional half errored on infrastructure, and the orchestrator's amendment rule B4 would normally push an audit with errored mandatory phases to `errored` (retry). It does not apply here, for two independent reasons:

1. **Rule B1 fires first and is unconditional** — "Any finding `severity = Critical` → NON-COMPLIANT, unconditionally." C1 and C2 are Critical and were established from the compose alone, with the static leaf run to completion.
2. **A retry cannot change the outcome.** `errored` is a retry state meaning "we could not tell". Here we can tell: at `main` there is no `docker-compose.yml`, so no demo host — however healthy its credentials — could install OpenClaw. The functional phases are unreachable for an app-attributable reason, not merely an infra one.
Calling this `errored` would misreport a parked app with two Critical defects as a transient harness failure.

## Required before re-enabling

1. **C1** — make `pre-install-cmd` idempotent: only write `openclaw.json` when absent (`[ -f /DATA/AppData/openclaw/openclaw.json ] || cat > …`), or merge into the existing file.
2. **C2** — migrate to the AppShield/OIDC sidecar per the CONTRIBUTING reference apps, and stop passing the secret in the `index` query string; if the `DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_DEVICE_AUTH` / `allowInsecureAuth` / `--allow-unconfigured` combination must be retained behind the proxy, ship a `rationale.md` covering exactly those three settings and the shell-execution blast radius.
3. **M3** — `chown` the AppData tree to `$PUID:$PGID` in `pre-install-cmd`, or set an explicit `user:` on the backend consistent with the directory it is handed.
4. **M2** — add `thumbnail.png` and its `x-casaos.thumbnail` URL.
5. **M1** — only then rename `docker-compose.yml.disabled` → `docker-compose.yml`, and re-run this audit at `depth=full` against a demo host with working credentials so Phases A–G produce real results.
## Audit caveats

- Phases A–G produced **no runtime evidence**; every runtime statement above is labelled as a static prediction.
- The GitHub REST API rate-limited this run (no token in this sandbox), so the specific later commit that reverted the compose to `.disabled` was not identified. The current state at `main` is nonetheless confirmed twice, by two different endpoints.
- Whether OpenClaw still appears in the live store UI was not visually confirmed, because store access is behind the failed login.
